faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.whatIs.question: What is Vikunja?
faq.whatIs.answer: Vikunja is an open-source, self-hostable to-do app. It helps you organize your tasks and projects with features like list, kanban, gantt, and table views — all while keeping your data under your control.
faq.free.question: Is Vikunja free and open source?
faq.free.answer: Yes. Vikunja is licensed under the AGPLv3 and completely free to self-host. If you prefer not to manage your own server, [Vikunja Cloud]({cloudLink}) offers a paid hosted option.
faq.install.question: How do I install Vikunja?
faq.install.answer: You can install Vikunja using Docker, native binaries for your platform, or sign up for [Vikunja Cloud]({cloudLink}). Use the [install wizard]({installUrl}) for a guided setup.
faq.selfHost.question: Do I have to self-host Vikunja?
faq.selfHost.answer: No. While self-hosting is a great option, [Vikunja Cloud]({cloudLink}) gives you a fully managed instance with automatic updates, backups, and zero maintenance. It's the easiest way to get started and directly supports the continued development of Vikunja.
faq.import.question: Can I import tasks from Todoist, Trello, or Microsoft To-Do?
faq.import.answer: Yes. Vikunja has built-in migration support for Todoist, Trello, Microsoft To-Do, and other platforms. You can import your existing tasks and projects directly from the Vikunja interface.

home.quote.cloud: Vikunja Cloud is the best way for me to make sure the project can continue to live on and be self-sustainable. Being completely bootstrapped, the users of the software are the top priority and not some VC.

features.description: Discover Vikunja, the open-source task management tool with powerful features. Stay organized, collaborate, and customize your workflow with multiple views.
features.hero.title: Think of Vikunja like the notebook you have with all your things to keep track of.
features.hero.subtitle: But with superpowers.
features.organized.title: Stay organized
features.organized.text: Organize all of your tasks in projects. Create subprojects to organize everything hierarchically and keep related stuff grouped together.
features.collaborate.title: Collaborate with peers
features.collaborate.text: Vikunja lets you easily share a project with another user or a whole team! Assignments show who's working on what.
features.flexible.title: Use it how you need it
features.flexible.text: You can view your tasks in the classic list view - or in a Gantt Chart, or Table view, or Kanban Board. Whatever you need!
features.openSource.title: Open Source
features.openSource.text: Vikunja is openly licensed under the {license}. You can contribute in multiple ways, even if you're not a developer! It already helps a lot when you use Vikunja and report features you'd like or bugs you find. And if you are a developer and know your way around Go or Vue.js, any help is appreciated.
features.speed.title: Built for speed.
features.speed.text: We built Vikunja with speed in mind - every interaction takes less than 100ms. No more loading spinners.
features.speed.text2: Because a productive tool should not get in your way.
features.tasks.alt: The image shows a minimalist task management interface with a numbered header, breadcrumb navigation, description field, and an embedded colorful abstract image.
features.tasks.title: Tasks
features.tasks.reminders: Tasks are not only simple tasks. You can let Vikunja remind you of tasks when they're due. Never miss an important deadline again!
features.tasks.repeating: Remember that thing you have to do every week but can't get the hang of it? You can set tasks to repeat in a time interval, letting Vikunja remind you of important weekly or monthly tasks.
features.tasks.subtasks: Vikunja also lets you split a task into multiple subtasks for easy progress tracking and more satisfaction when crossing them off the list!
features.quickAdd.title: Quick Add Magic
features.quickAdd.text: Add a task with a due date, labels, assignees and more without having to edit it afterwards?
features.quickAdd.text2: Vikunja's Quick Add Magic lets you do just that! Simply create a task mentioning a date, and it will add it as a due date. Or use one of the special keywords to automatically add labels, assignees and more.
features.views.title: View your tasks in whatever way you like
features.views.text: Vikunja allows you to view tasks in four different views - use whatever works best for you.
features.list.alt: A task management interface displaying an input field to add new tasks, followed by a list of sample tasks with checkboxes, due dates, assignments, labels, and a "Quick Add Magic" feature.
features.list.title: List
features.list.text: The list view is similar to a classic to-do list in a lot of ways. It shows you all tasks in a list underneath each other, enriched with all other task attributes Vikunja has to offer.
features.gantt.alt: Calendar view for July 2022 showing three blue task cards scheduled across different dates and a "Create a new task" button at the bottom.
features.gantt.title: Gantt Chart
features.gantt.text: The Gantt Chart is perfect to get a timely overview of all tasks currently in-progress in a project. It allows for easy planning of deadlines and due dates.
features.kanban.alt: A Kanban-style task board showing two columns, "Backlog" and "Doing", with various numbered task cards containing descriptions, labels, and status indicators.
features.kanban.title: Kanban board
features.kanban.text: Vikunja lets you organize and prioritize your tasks in a kanban board. Quickly get an overview of the status of things - especially when collaborating with multiple people on a project.
features.kanban.text2: Each card on a board represents a task in Vikunja. All tasks can be added through the usual ways and will then show up in the kanban board where they can be easily rearranged and reordered.
features.table.alt: A task list interface showing numbered tasks with titles, completion status, and labels in a sortable table format.
features.table.title: Table
features.table.text: With the table view, you can see all task details of all your tasks. And you can even change what task attributes should be visible!
features.import.title: Import your tasks from Todoist, Trello or Microsoft To-Do
features.import.text: Because work does not happen in one tool only.
features.other.title: Other Features
features.other.labels.title: Labels
features.other.labels.text: Effortlessly mark tasks with a colorful label to find and group relevant tasks with a click!
features.other.filters.title: Saved Filters
features.other.filters.text: Create a filter with only the tasks you care about. Save it once, use it always.
features.other.priorities.title: Priorities
features.other.priorities.text: Know that feeling when you have a dozen things to do but can't decide on what to work next? Vikunja lets you quickly prioritize your tasks, so you'll always know on what to work next.
features.other.delegation.title: Delegation
features.other.delegation.text: Assign tasks to other users or yourself so everyone always knows who is responsible for which task.
features.other.attachments.title: Attachments
features.other.attachments.text: Attach files to tasks, so you can always have all related files for a task in one place!
features.other.relations.title: Relations
features.other.relations.text: Relate different tasks together - even if they're not in the same project! A relation can be multiple things, for example a subtask or blocking task.
features.other.dueDates.title: Due dates
features.other.dueDates.text: Remember these tasks with a deadline coming up? Set a due date for a task and see all tasks with upcoming deadlines at once!
features.other.shareLinks.title: Share links
features.other.shareLinks.text: You can share a project with a link so that others can directly see or edit all tasks in a project but don't need to create an account. Share links have all the same rights management as sharing with users or teams.
features.other.caldav.text: Vikunja comes with a calDAV-integration which lets you use the tools you already use and love.
features.privacy.title: We will never look at your tasks.
features.privacy.text: We will never sell your grocery list or metadata. Because privacy matters.
features.privacy.text2: Don't take our word for it, {checkIt}! Vikunja is openly licensed under the AGPLv3.

plans.whyNoFree.title: Why is there no free version?
plans.whyNoFree.cost: Building and maintaining software costs money and time. There's no way around it. That money has to come from {somewhere}. Most free products either have limited functionality to nag you to buy a premium version that is actually usable or just sell your data to advertising companies. In those cases, you're not the user, you're the product.
plans.whyNoFree.notUs: We don't do any of this.
plans.whyNoFree.userFirst: We believe you, the user, should be front and center of the software you're using. You're always free to host Vikunja yourself, no strings attached. Keep in mind that also means you will need to take care of all server maintenance, updates and backups yourself. If that's your jam, great! But if you just want to use it, consider buying a subscription to support the ongoing development.
plans.whyNoFree.trial: If you're not sure Vikunja is useful to you, just try it risk-free with a 14-day trial. Feel free to {reachOut} if you have any questions.

pricing.description: Vikunja pricing for individuals, teams, and enterprises. Self-host for free or let us run it for you. Enterprise features without the enterprise price tag.

pricing.hero.subtitle: Self-host Vikunja for free, forever. Or let us handle the infrastructure so you can focus on your tasks.
pricing.comparison.title: Self-Hosted vs. Cloud vs. Pro
pricing.comparison.import: Import from Todoist, Trello, MS To-Do
pricing.faq.free.question: Is the self-hosted version really free?
pricing.faq.free.answer: Yes. Vikunja is openly licensed under the [AGPLv3]({licenseUrl}). You can self-host it for personal use or for your entire company at no cost. All core features are included.
pricing.faq.cloudVsSelfHosted.question: What does Vikunja Cloud give me that self-hosting doesn't?
pricing.faq.cloudVsSelfHosted.answer: The same features, minus the ops work. We handle hosting, backups, updates, and TLS. You get a managed instance hosted in the EU, so you can focus on your tasks instead of your infrastructure.
pricing.faq.family.question: Is there a family plan?
pricing.faq.family.answer: Yes. The Cloud Family plan covers up to 5 users for 10€/month or 99€/year — one subscription for the whole household, fully managed by us. If you self-host instead, the [Pro Homelab plan]({proUrl}) brings Pro features to your own instance at a flat fee for up to 5 users.
pricing.faq.whatIsPro.question: What is Vikunja Pro?
pricing.faq.whatIsPro.answer: Pro adds features like an admin panel, audit logs, and time tracking to a Vikunja instance you host yourself. It's a separate product from Vikunja Cloud: Cloud plans are on this page, Pro plans are on the [Pro page]({proUrl}). Pro features will come to Cloud eventually, but as a separate offering — the current Pro plans don't apply to Cloud accounts.
pricing.faq.trial.question: Can I try before I buy?
pricing.faq.trial.answer: Every Cloud plan comes with a free 14-day trial. Cancel anytime. You can also [try the live demo]({demoUrl}) right now without signing up.
pricing.faq.switch.question: Can I switch from self-hosted to Cloud (or the other way around)?
pricing.faq.switch.answer: Yes. You can export your data and import it into another instance. If you need help migrating, [reach out]({contactUrl}) and we'll walk you through it.
pricing.faq.atWork.question: I'm already self-hosting. How do I bring Vikunja to my team at work?
pricing.faq.atWork.answer: Check out the [Convince Your Boss]({convinceUrl}) page — it has everything you need to make the case internally.

pro.adds.adminPanel: Manage users, teams, and permissions from a central interface. No more poking at the database.
pro.adds.auditLogs: Real audit trails you can integrate with external systems. Compliance-grade, not decorative.
pro.adds.timeTracking: Track time spent on tasks directly in Vikunja. No separate tool, no context switching.
pro.adds.guestUsers.title: Guest users
pro.adds.guestUsers: Invite clients and external collaborators into single projects without giving them a full seat on your instance.
pro.adds.clientInvoicing: Turn tracked time into client invoices without leaving Vikunja. No spreadsheet detour.
pro.openSource.title: Still open source. Still yours.
pro.openSource.license.title: Same license
pro.openSource.license.text: AGPLv3. Not "source available." Not "open core." The real thing. Every line of code, {auditable}.
pro.openSource.adds.title: Pro adds, it doesn't take away
pro.openSource.adds.text: The free version stays exactly as it is. Pro adds features on top. Nothing is being removed or paywalled from what's already there.
pro.openSource.lockIn.title: No lock-in
pro.openSource.lockIn.text: If you cancel, the core app keeps running and your data stays yours. Pro features deactivate, but you're never locked out of your own work.
pro.openSource.community.title: Same community
pro.openSource.community.text: Bug reports, feature requests, and contributions work exactly the same way. Pro customers don't get a separate roadmap.
pro.quote.text: "I built Vikunja because I believe you should own your tools. That doesn't change because you want to share it with your family or your team."
pro.convince.text: Already using Vikunja at home and want to bring it to work? {link}
pro.convince.link: Here's everything you need to make the case.
pro.cta.text: Vikunja Pro is currently in private beta. Join the waitlist and we'll be in touch.
pro.cta.waitlistNote: The waitlist is for the self-hosted Pro plans above. If you'd rather have us do the hosting, {cloudLink} is available today, no waitlist needed.
pro.faq.familyCloud.question: Is this a family plan for Vikunja Cloud?
pro.faq.familyCloud.answer: No — but that exists! Vikunja Cloud has a [Family plan]({pricingUrl}): up to 5 users on a fully managed instance for 10€/month or 99€/year, available today, no waitlist. The Pro Homelab plan is something else: it adds Pro features to a Vikunja instance you host yourself. We plan to bring Pro features to Cloud eventually, but that will be a separate offering with its own pricing, not the plans on this page.
pro.faq.openCore.question: Is this open core?
pro.faq.openCore.answer: No. The existing Vikunja stays exactly as it is. Nothing is being taken away or locked behind a paywall. Pro adds new features (like audit logs, an admin panel, and time tracking) on top. All of it is AGPLv3.
pro.faq.stopPaying.question: What if I stop paying?
pro.faq.stopPaying.answer: Vikunja itself keeps working. Your tasks, projects, and data aren't going anywhere. The Pro features (audit logs, admin panel, time tracking) need an active subscription. The core app you use every day does not.
pro.faq.planDifference.question: What's the difference between the plans?
pro.faq.planDifference.answer: Homelab is a flat fee for up to 5 users, for people running Vikunja on their own server at home. It includes the admin panel and time tracking, but no audit logs and no guest users. Team is for small teams: up to 25 users on a single instance, plus 5 guest users, still without audit logs. Business adds audit logs, unlimited guests, and client invoicing, for up to 500 users across up to 3 instances. Scale is Business without the ceilings: unlimited users and unlimited instances. Enterprise is for organizations that need yearly invoicing, a GDPR data processing agreement, or hands-on support via phone. If you'd rather not run the instance yourself, a managed dedicated instance is available as a paid add-on on any plan.
pro.faq.perUserBilling.question: How does per-user billing work?
pro.faq.perUserBilling.answer: On the Team, Business, and Scale plans you choose one of two models: set a fixed number of seats and add or remove them at any time, or let us automatically bill for the number of users active on your instance, with no seat management needed. Monthly and yearly billing are both available.
pro.faq.guestUsers.question: What are guest users?
pro.faq.guestUsers.answer: Guest users are people you invite into individual projects without giving them a full seat on your instance — clients, freelancers, or anyone who only needs to see their own corner of the work. Team includes 5 guests, Business and up are unlimited, and Homelab doesn't include them. This feature is still being built.
pro.faq.clientInvoicing.question: What is client invoicing?
pro.faq.clientInvoicing.answer: Client invoicing turns the time you already track in Vikunja into an invoice: pick a client and a period, and Vikunja builds it from your time tracking data — no spreadsheet detour. It's included from the Business plan up and is still being built.
pro.faq.selfHost.question: Can I self-host with a Pro plan?
pro.faq.selfHost.answer: Yes. All Pro plans work with self-hosted Vikunja. Sign up, get your license key, add it to your instance. That's it.
pro.faq.alreadySelfHosting.question: I'm already self-hosting Vikunja for free. What changes?
pro.faq.alreadySelfHosting.answer: Nothing has to change. The free self-hosted version isn't going anywhere. Pro adds features on top of what's already there. It doesn't take anything away.
pro.faq.licenseKey.question: If it's AGPLv3, why do I need a license key?
pro.faq.licenseKey.answer: All Pro feature code lives in the same repo under the same AGPLv3 license. Nothing is hidden or proprietary. The license key activates the features so they work out of the box. You're paying for a working product and for continued development of the project.
pro.faq.everyFeaturePro.question: Does this mean every new feature will be Pro from now on?
pro.faq.everyFeaturePro.answer: No. Pro features are things that companies genuinely need and are happy to pay for because it helps them run their business: time tracking, audit logs, admin tooling. Regular task management features keep landing in the free version like they always have.
pro.faq.sellOut.question: Is this a sell-out?
pro.faq.sellOut.answer: No. This is how the project stays sustainable without VC money, ads, or selling your data. Every subscription funds continued development of the same open-source project everyone uses.
pro.faq.vsCloud.question: How is this different from Vikunja Cloud?
pro.faq.vsCloud.answer: They're two separate products. Vikunja Cloud is managed hosting: we run Vikunja for you, and you pay for the hosting. Pro is a feature upgrade for an instance you run yourself. Pro features will come to Cloud eventually, but as a different offering with its own pricing — not the plans on this page.
pro.faq.privateBeta.question: What does "private beta" mean?
pro.faq.privateBeta.answer: It means we're ironing out the last bugs before general availability. You can use it in production, but expect some rough edges. Pricing and features may still change before GA.
pro.faq.trial.question: Can I try before I buy?
pro.faq.trial.answer: Yes. Every Pro plan comes with a free trial.
pro.faq.cloudUser.question: I'm on Vikunja Cloud. Can I get Pro features?
pro.faq.cloudUser.answer: Not yet. Pro is currently available for self-hosted and dedicated instances only. Pro features will come to Cloud eventually, but as a separate offering — joining the Pro waitlist won't get you early access on Cloud.
pro.faq.sso.question: What about SSO and LDAP?
pro.faq.sso.answer: Already included in the free version of Vikunja. You don't need Pro for that. See the setup docs for [OpenID Connect]({openidUrl}) and [LDAP]({ldapUrl}).
pro.faq.nonProfit.question: Do you offer a non-profit discount?
pro.faq.nonProfit.answer: Yes. If you're a registered non-profit, [drop us an email]({contactUrl}) and we'll sort it out.
pro.faq.ppp.question: Do you offer purchasing power parity (PPP)?
pro.faq.ppp.answer: Yes. If you're in a country where the standard pricing doesn't make sense, [send us an email]({contactUrl}) and we'll work something out.

convince.pitch.title: The pitch in 30 seconds
convince.pitch.p1: Vikunja is open-source task management that runs on your infrastructure. It replaces Todoist, Trello, or Asana for teams that need full control over their data.
convince.pitch.p2: Your team gets lists, Kanban boards, Gantt charts, and table views, with shared projects, assignments, and real-time collaboration. Enterprise features like a dedicated instance, admin tools, and a GDPR data processing agreement are available at any team size. No minimum seat count.
convince.pitch.p3: It's made and hosted in the EU, openly licensed under the AGPLv3, and completely bootstrapped. Funded by users, not VCs.
convince.why.title: Why switch from what we already use?
convince.why.data.title: Your data stays yours
convince.why.data.text: Self-host on your own infrastructure or use our EU-hosted cloud. No data leaves your control. No US cloud provider in the chain. Full GDPR compliance with a data processing agreement available.
convince.why.lockIn.title: No vendor lock-in
convince.why.lockIn.text: Open-source under the AGPLv3 means you can read every line of code, export your data anytime, and switch hosting providers without losing anything. You're never locked into a contract you can't leave.
convince.why.enterprise.title: Enterprise features without the enterprise price tag
convince.why.enterprise.text: Dedicated instances, admin user management, and GDPR contracts don't require 25+ users or a six-figure budget. Your compliance requirements don't care how many employees you have. Neither does Vikunja's pricing.
convince.why.views.title: One tool, four views
convince.why.views.text: List, Kanban, Gantt, and Table. Your team doesn't have to pick one workflow. Developers can use Kanban while project managers use Gantt, all looking at the same data.

convince.security.title: Security and compliance
convince.security.openSource.title: Open source
convince.security.openSource.text: Every line of Vikunja's code is publicly auditable under the AGPLv3. No hidden telemetry, no proprietary black boxes.
convince.security.eu.title: Made and hosted in the EU
convince.security.eu.text: Vikunja is built in Germany and hosted on EU infrastructure. No data transfers to the US. No CLOUD Act exposure.
convince.security.gdpr.title: GDPR-ready
convince.security.gdpr.text: Data processing agreements are available on the Enterprise plan. Self-hosted instances give you complete control over data residency.
convince.security.disclosure.title: Responsible disclosure
convince.security.disclosure.text: Security vulnerabilities are handled through a {disclosureLink} with published advisories and CVEs.
convince.deploy.title: Deployment options
convince.deploy.intro: Pick what fits your team's infrastructure:
convince.deploy.docker.text: Single container, one command. The fastest way to get running. Works on any server with Docker installed.
convince.deploy.kubernetes.text: Helm chart available for production Kubernetes clusters. Scale horizontally as your team grows.
convince.deploy.cloud.text: Don't want to manage infrastructure? We'll host it for you on EU servers. Enterprise plans get a dedicated instance.
convince.pilot.title: Run a team pilot
convince.pilot.intro: The best way to evaluate Vikunja is to use it with your team for two weeks. Here's how:
convince.pilot.people.title: Pick 5–10 people
convince.pilot.people.text: a mix of roles that represent how your team actually works.
convince.pilot.setup.title: Set up a test instance
convince.pilot.import.title: Import existing tasks
convince.pilot.import.text: bring in your data from Todoist, Trello, or Microsoft To-Do.
convince.pilot.realWork.title: Use it for real work
convince.pilot.realWork.text: run your actual sprint, project, or team tasks through Vikunja for two weeks.
convince.pilot.evaluate.title: Evaluate
convince.pilot.evaluate.text: does it cover your workflow? Is your team using it without being reminded?
convince.cta.title: Ready to get started?
convince.cta.text: Have questions about Enterprise or need help scoping a pilot?
compare.common.schemaDescription: Side-by-side comparison of Vikunja and {name} for task management.
compare.common.whyAlternatives: Why people are looking for alternatives
compare.common.cloudPricing: If you'd rather not manage a server, {cloud} starts at 4 €/month for personal use and 5 €/user/month for teams, hosted on EU infrastructure.
compare.todoist.title: Vikunja vs Todoist: The Self-Hosted Alternative
compare.todoist.description: Todoist alternative you can self-host. Lists, labels, reminders, Kanban, Gantt. On your server, not theirs. Open-source, EU-hosted, no task limits on the free plan.
compare.todoist.subtitle: Your to-do list, your server.
compare.todoist.intro1: Todoist is a good task manager. Millions of people use it. But it's closed-source, hosted in the US, and increasingly aggressive about what it locks behind a paywall.
compare.todoist.intro2: {limits} And your data sits on Doist's servers in San Francisco whether you like it or not.
compare.todoist.intro2Limits: Reminders? Paid. More than 5 projects? Paid. More than 300 tasks in a project? Paid. File attachments? Paid.
compare.todoist.intro3: Vikunja gives you the same workflow you already know from Todoist: lists, labels, due dates, reminders, quick add with natural language. But it runs on your server. You can read every line of the code. And the free self-hosted version has no limits on projects, tasks, or features.
compare.todoist.intro4: If you don't want to manage a server, {cloud} runs it for you on EU infrastructure. Either way, your team's project planning doesn't depend on a service you have zero control over.
compare.todoist.extras.title: What you get that Todoist doesn't offer
compare.todoist.extras.intro: Beyond the self-hosting, there are a few things Vikunja does that Todoist simply can't.
compare.todoist.extras.views.title: Four views, not one
compare.todoist.extras.views.text: Todoist is a list app. Vikunja shows the same tasks as a {views}. Your project manager can use Gantt while your developers use Kanban. Same data, different lens.
compare.todoist.extras.views.link: list, Kanban board, Gantt chart, or table
compare.todoist.extras.caldav.title: CalDAV built in
compare.todoist.extras.caldav.text: Vikunja speaks {caldav}, so it works with the calendar and to-do apps you already use. Todoist has no CalDAV support at all.
compare.todoist.extras.limits.title: No artificial limits
compare.todoist.extras.limits.text: Self-hosted Vikunja doesn't cap your projects at 5 or your tasks at 300. Unlimited {projects}, unlimited tasks, unlimited {filters}, unlimited {labels}. No upgrade nags.
compare.todoist.pricing.text1: Self-hosted Vikunja is free and always will be. If you'd rather not manage a server, {cloud} starts at 4 €/month (40 €/year) for personal use and 5 €/user/month for teams.
compare.todoist.pricing.text2: For reference, {competitor} (billed yearly). But the real difference isn't the price tag. It's that Vikunja doesn't paywall basic features like reminders, attachments, and filters behind a paid plan.
compare.todoist.pricing.competitor: Todoist Pro is $5/month and Business is $8/user/month
compare.todoist.switch.intro: Vikunja has a built-in Todoist importer. The whole process takes about 10 minutes:
compare.todoist.switch.step2: Go to Settings, connect your Todoist account, and pick the projects you want
compare.todoist.switch.step3: Your tasks, labels, and due dates come over automatically
compare.todoist.switch.outro: Try it for a week with your real tasks. If it works, cancel Todoist.
compare.todoist.faq.import.question: Can I import my Todoist tasks into Vikunja?
compare.todoist.faq.import.answer: Yes. Vikunja has a [built-in Todoist importer]({importUrl}). Connect your account, pick the projects you want, and your tasks, labels, and due dates come over automatically.
compare.todoist.faq.quickAdd.question: Does Vikunja have Quick Add like Todoist?
compare.todoist.faq.quickAdd.answer: Yes. [Quick Add Magic]({quickAddUrl}) lets you type a task with a due date, labels, assignees, and priority inline, similar to Todoist's natural language input.
compare.todoist.faq.reminders.question: Does Vikunja have reminders?
compare.todoist.faq.reminders.answer: Yes, on all plans, including the free self-hosted version. Check out [how reminders work]({remindersUrl}). Todoist paywalls reminders behind the Pro plan.
compare.todoist.faq.mobile.question: What about mobile apps?
compare.todoist.faq.mobile.answer: Vikunja works as a progressive web app on any device. Native apps are on the roadmap.
compare.trello.title: Vikunja vs Trello: Self-Hosted Kanban and Beyond
compare.trello.description: Trello alternative with Kanban, Gantt, list, and table views. Self-host it or use our EU cloud. No Power-Up tax, no Atlassian lock-in.
compare.trello.schemaDescription: Side-by-side comparison of Vikunja and Trello for task and project management.
compare.trello.subtitle: Kanban boards that aren't owned by Atlassian.
compare.trello.intro1: Trello popularized Kanban boards for everyone. Then Atlassian bought it, and now you pay {calendar}.
compare.trello.intro2: On the free plan, you get {limits}. Want more views? Premium. Custom fields? Standard plan. {csv} The free tier is a demo with guardrails.
compare.trello.intro2Limits: 10 boards and 250 automation runs per month
compare.trello.intro3: Vikunja has Kanban boards. It also has {views} of the same data. All of them work on every plan, including the free self-hosted one. No Power-Ups required.
compare.trello.intro4: And because it's open-source, you can run it on your own server. Your project boards don't live on Atlassian's US infrastructure. You can put them wherever you want.
compare.trello.paid.title: What Trello makes you pay for
compare.trello.paid.intro: These are free in Vikunja. All of them.
compare.trello.paid.views: {title} Trello's calendar, timeline, table, and dashboard views are {locked} ($10/user/month). In Vikunja, you {switch} whenever you want.
compare.trello.paid.viewsSwitch: switch between list, Kanban, Gantt, and table
compare.trello.paid.csv: {title} Trello {premiumOnly}. On the free plan, your only option is a JSON dump. Vikunja lets you export your data on any plan, because it's your data.
compare.trello.paid.csvPremiumOnly: only lets Premium users export to CSV
compare.trello.paid.boards: {title} Trello's free plan {caps} per workspace. Vikunja has no limits on projects.
compare.trello.paid.eu: {title} Trello doesn't support Atlassian's data residency feature. Your data is in the US, period. With Vikunja, self-host wherever you want, or use our Cloud on EU infrastructure.
compare.trello.pricing.text1: Self-hosted Vikunja is free and always will be. {cloud} starts at 5 €/user/month for teams.
compare.trello.pricing.text2: For reference, {competitor} (billed yearly). You need Premium for calendar, timeline, and table views. Enterprise requires a minimum of 25 users. Vikunja has no seat minimums on any plan.
compare.trello.pricing.competitor: Trello Standard is $5/user/month and Premium is $10/user/month
compare.trello.switch.step2: Export your Trello board as JSON (Menu → More → Print and Export)
compare.trello.switch.step3: Import the JSON file in Vikunja's migration settings
compare.trello.switch.outro: Your cards, lists, and labels come over. Try it for a week with real work.
compare.trello.faq.import.question: Can I import my Trello boards?
compare.trello.faq.import.answer: Yes. Export your board as JSON from Trello, then [import it in Vikunja]({importUrl}). Your cards, lists, and labels come over automatically.
compare.trello.faq.automations.question: Does Vikunja have automations like Trello's Butler?
compare.trello.faq.automations.answer: Vikunja supports [webhooks]({webhooksUrl}) that let you trigger external automations. It doesn't have a visual automation builder like Butler, but the webhook approach is more flexible if you're comfortable with tools like n8n or Zapier.
compare.trello.faq.free.question: Can I use Vikunja for free?
compare.trello.faq.free.answer: Self-host it for free with no limits on boards, tasks, or users. If you want managed hosting, [Vikunja Cloud]({cloudLink}) starts at 4 EUR/month with a 14-day free trial.
compare.notion.title: Vikunja vs Notion: Fast Task Management You Can Self-Host
compare.notion.description: Notion alternative for teams that just need task management. Four views, sub-100ms speed, self-hostable. No bloat, no slow loading, no US-only data.
compare.notion.subtitle: A task manager that loads in milliseconds, not seconds.
compare.notion.intro1: Notion tries to be everything. Docs, wiki, database, project manager, AI assistant. And if you need all of that, it's a reasonable choice.
compare.notion.intro2: But if what you actually need is a task manager? Notion is slow. Pages take seconds to load. The mobile app is sluggish. And you're paying {price} for a tool where you mostly use one feature.
compare.notion.intro3: Vikunja does task management. That's it. {views}. Every interaction takes less than 100ms. It's fast because it's focused.
compare.notion.intro4: It's also open-source and self-hostable. Notion keeps your data on US servers ({eu}). Vikunja lets you run it wherever you want, or use our Cloud on EU infrastructure.
compare.notion.jobs.title: Different tools, different jobs
compare.notion.jobs.intro: This isn't an apples-to-apples comparison. Notion does more things. But for task management specifically, here's how they stack up.
compare.notion.pricing.text1: Self-hosted Vikunja is free. {cloud} starts at 4 €/month for personal use and 5 €/user/month for teams. {competitor} (billed yearly).
compare.notion.pricing.competitor: Notion Plus starts at $10/user/month, Business at $18/user/month
compare.notion.pricing.text2: But these are different tools solving different problems. If you need a full workspace with docs, wikis, and databases, Notion's price covers a lot more surface area. If you need a fast task manager you can self-host, Vikunja is the better fit regardless of what it costs.
compare.notion.which.title: When to pick which
compare.notion.which.vikunja: {pick} if you need a task manager that's fast, self-hostable, and respects your data. Especially if you're a team that's been using Notion for tasks but finds it slow, expensive, or overkill for what you actually do with it.
compare.notion.which.notion: {pick} if you genuinely need the wiki, docs, and database features. If your team lives in Notion for documentation and project context, adding task management on top makes sense even if it's slower.
compare.notion.which.both: Some teams use both: Notion for docs and knowledge, Vikunja for the actual task tracking.
compare.notion.faq.replacement.question: Is Vikunja a Notion replacement?
compare.notion.faq.replacement.answer: Not really. Notion is a workspace with wikis, docs, and databases. Vikunja is a task manager. If your team uses Notion mainly for task tracking, Vikunja does that part better and faster. If you need the wiki and database features, you'll want to keep Notion or pair Vikunja with something like Outline or BookStack.
compare.notion.faq.import.question: Can I import from Notion?
compare.notion.faq.import.answer: There's no direct importer, but you can export Notion databases as CSV and restructure them in Vikunja. If you're also on Todoist or Trello, those have [built-in importers]({importUrl}).
compare.notion.faq.docs.question: Does Vikunja have docs or a wiki?
compare.notion.faq.docs.answer: No. Every task has a rich-text description with markdown support, but Vikunja is a task manager, not a documentation tool.
compare.wekan.title: Vikunja vs WeKan: A Stable Alternative for Self-Hosters
compare.wekan.description: Looking for a WeKan alternative? Vikunja is an open-source, self-hosted task manager with Kanban, Gantt, and table views, plus a built-in WeKan importer to bring your boards over in minutes.
compare.wekan.schemaDescription: Side-by-side comparison of Vikunja and WeKan for self-hosted task and project management.
compare.wekan.subtitle: Looking for a new home for your boards? Here's how they compare.
compare.wekan.intro1: WeKan has been one of the go-to open-source Kanban boards for a long time, and for good reason. But the project has been going through a rough stretch. The v8 release introduced CSS changes that {layouts} for many users, and features like {sso} and {labels} have had regressions in recent releases. Maintaining open-source software solo is hard (I know the feeling), and these things happen. But if your team depends on their board every day, you need something stable.
compare.wekan.intro2: I built Vikunja because I wanted a self-hosted task manager I could rely on. It does everything WeKan does and quite a bit more: lists, Kanban, Gantt charts, tables, CalDAV, reminders, and a full REST API. It ships as a single Go binary with SQLite, so it's lightweight to run and straightforward to maintain.
compare.wekan.intro3: There's a {importer} that brings your boards over in minutes. Export your board as JSON in WeKan, upload it in Vikunja, done. Tasks, labels, and buckets come across in one go.
compare.wekan.why.intro: These are some of the concerns WeKan users have raised on GitHub:
compare.wekan.why.quote1: "Many of us have end users depending on WeKan daily. When the UI breaks, they flood us with support requests."
compare.wekan.why.quote2: "Latest versions UI is broken [...] and it looks like a samsung smartphone UI or something that is just not professional."
compare.wekan.changes.updates.title: Updates you can actually install
compare.wekan.changes.updates.text: Every Vikunja release has a {changelog}. Breaking changes are documented before they land. Upgrades don't hang your database or break your login screen. You stop treating "don't touch it" as an ops strategy.
compare.wekan.changes.views.title: Four views, not just Kanban
compare.wekan.changes.views.text: WeKan gives you a Kanban board. Vikunja gives you {views} on the same data. Your project manager uses Gantt while your developers use Kanban. Switch between them anytime.
compare.wekan.changes.ui.title: A clean, consistent UI
compare.wekan.changes.ui.text: Vikunja's interface is designed for desktop and mobile alike. It looks clean, stays consistent across updates, and won't surprise your team after an upgrade.
compare.wekan.changes.lightweight.text: Vikunja is a single Go binary. No Meteor, no Node.js runtime, no MongoDB. It runs on SQLite by default and uses around 50 MB of RAM. It'll happily run on a Raspberry Pi alongside the rest of your homelab.
compare.wekan.changes.api.title: CalDAV and a full API
compare.wekan.changes.api.text: {caldav} means your tasks show up in Thunderbird, Apple Reminders, or any CalDAV client. The {api} has full OpenAPI docs, so you can integrate Vikunja into your existing workflows.
compare.wekan.table.ramWekan: 500 MB+ (maintainer recommends 64 GB for larger installs)
compare.wekan.pricing.bothFree: Both Vikunja and WeKan are free and open source for self-hosting.
compare.wekan.pricing.text2: The bigger difference is operational: Vikunja is a single binary with SQLite, while WeKan requires MongoDB and Node.js, which means more resources on your server. If you're running a homelab or a small VPS, that matters.
compare.wekan.switch.intro: The whole process takes a few minutes per board:
compare.wekan.switch.step2: In WeKan, export each board as JSON (board menu > Export board > JSON)
compare.wekan.switch.step3: In Vikunja, go to the import page and upload your JSON files
compare.wekan.switch.step4: Your tasks, labels, and buckets come across automatically
compare.wekan.switch.outro: Try it with one board first. If it works the way you expect, bring the rest over. Check the {guide} for the full walkthrough.
compare.wekan.cta.text: Import one WeKan board and see how it feels. If it works, bring the rest over.
compare.wekan.faq.import.question: Can I import my WeKan boards into Vikunja?
compare.wekan.faq.import.answer: Yes. Export your WeKan board as JSON (board menu > Export board > JSON), then upload it on Vikunja's [import page]({importUrl}). Tasks, labels, and buckets all come across in one go.
compare.wekan.faq.kanban.question: Does Vikunja have Kanban boards like WeKan?
compare.wekan.faq.kanban.answer: Yes, and more. Vikunja supports [four views]({viewsUrl}): List, Kanban, Gantt, and Table. You can switch between them anytime. Same data, different perspective.
compare.wekan.faq.swimlanes.question: Does Vikunja support swimlanes?
compare.wekan.faq.swimlanes.answer: Vikunja's Kanban view uses buckets (columns) that you can create and reorder freely. If you need to organize cards across multiple dimensions, you can use [labels]({labelsUrl}) and [saved filters]({filtersUrl}) to slice your data however you need.
compare.wekan.faq.server.question: Can I self-host Vikunja on the same server where WeKan runs?
compare.wekan.faq.server.answer: Yes. Vikunja runs as a single binary or Docker container. It uses SQLite by default (no separate database server needed), or PostgreSQL/MySQL if you prefer. It'll use a fraction of the resources WeKan needs. See the [installation guide]({installUrl}).
compare.wekan.faq.mobile.question: What about mobile access?
compare.wekan.faq.mobile.answer: Vikunja works as a progressive web app on any device. You can also access your tasks via [CalDAV]({caldavUrl}), which means they show up in your phone's native calendar and to-do apps.
compare.wekan.faq.data.question: Will my WeKan data come across cleanly?
compare.wekan.faq.data.answer: The importer brings over your tasks, labels, and buckets. You'll want to double-check a board or two after import, but in most cases everything lands where you expect it.
compare.planka.title: Vikunja vs Planka: Self-Hosted Kanban With SSO That Stays Free
compare.planka.description: Looking for a Planka alternative after SSO moved to Pro? Vikunja is an open-source, self-hosted task manager with Kanban, Gantt, List, and Table views. OIDC and LDAP are in the free version and stay there.
compare.planka.schemaDescription: Side-by-side comparison of Vikunja and Planka for self-hosted Kanban and project management.
compare.planka.subtitle: Self-hosted Kanban with SSO that stays in the free version.
compare.planka.intro1: Planka is a good Kanban board. It is fast, looks clean, and a lot of homelabs and small teams run it. In August 2026 the project {moved} and into the closed-source Pro tier. Version 2.2.0 shipped without it, and users who only ever logged in via SSO were deactivated on upgrade.
compare.planka.intro1Moved: moved OIDC/SSO out of the Community edition
compare.planka.intro2: The maintainers have been open about their reasoning: SSO generated a lot of support requests and they see it as an enterprise feature. That's a legitimate business call for them to make. For Vikunja, that line is somewhere else: your requirements (compliance or otherwise) don't care how many users you have, and a login method shouldn't be the thing that decides which tier you're on.
compare.planka.intro3: Vikunja is an open-source, self-hosted task manager with Kanban, List, Gantt, and Table views. {openid} and {ldap} are freely available, documented, and have been for years. There is a paid {pro}, but it ships in the same public repository under the same AGPL-3 license, and authentication isn't part of it.
compare.planka.intro4: There's also a {importer}: it pulls your boards straight out of Planka's REST API. It's in unstable builds now and ships with the next release. More on that below.
compare.planka.why.intro: From the GitHub thread announcing the SSO change:
compare.planka.why.quote1: "Security features, SSO or 2FA or auto-logout are in my opinion basic features and should not be put behind a paywall"
compare.planka.why.quote2: "I'm not expecting new versions to remove basic features."
compare.planka.why.quote3: "After updating to 2.2.0, all SSO-based users are deactivated, since they no longer have a password login."
compare.planka.changes.sso.title: SSO is a login button
compare.planka.changes.sso.text: {oidc} and {ldap} work in the free, self-hosted version. Point Vikunja at Authentik, Keycloak, Authelia, or your existing directory and log in. Users who come in via OIDC are regular users with the same permissions as anyone else.
compare.planka.changes.license.title: A license that keeps it that way
compare.planka.changes.license.text: Vikunja is AGPL-3 with no contributor license agreement. That means it's a constraint: I don't hold the rights I would need to move contributed code into a closed tier. Vikunja Pro exists and ships in the same public repo under the same license. {link}.
compare.planka.changes.license.link: Longer explanation of how that works is here
compare.planka.changes.views.title: Kanban and three more views
compare.planka.changes.views.text: Planka gives you a Kanban board. Vikunja gives you {views} on the same data. View all tasks in all different ways, switch between them anytime.
compare.planka.changes.data.title: Your data goes with you
compare.planka.changes.data.text: Vikunja has a {export} built in: projects, tasks, attachments, everything in one ZIP. If you ever want to leave, you can. Planka currently has {noExport}.
compare.planka.changes.lightweight.text: Vikunja is a single Go binary. It runs on SQLite by default, or PostgreSQL and MySQL if you prefer, and it's happy on a Raspberry Pi alongside the rest of your homelab.
compare.planka.changes.api.title: CalDAV, mobile, and a full API
compare.planka.changes.api.text: {caldav} puts your tasks in Thunderbird, Apple Reminders, or any CalDAV client. Vikunja works as a progressive web app on your phone, and the {api} has full OpenAPI docs.
compare.planka.table.licensePlanka: Source-available "PLANKA Community License"; Pro is closed source; contributors sign a CLA
compare.planka.table.dataExportPlanka: No native export ({issue}), REST API only
compare.planka.table.paidTierVikunja: Pro, same public repo, same license
compare.planka.pricing.text1: Both Vikunja and Planka Community are free to self-host. The difference is where the paid line sits. Planka Pro is a separate closed-source product and, since 2.2.0, it's where SSO lives. Vikunja Pro adds features on top of the free version but leaves authentication where it is.
compare.planka.switch.intro: Vikunja's Planka importer connects to your running Planka instance, so you don't need an export file (Planka doesn't have one anyway):
compare.planka.switch.step1: If your admin was SSO-only and you're locked out after 2.2.0, {link} first so you can reach your data
compare.planka.switch.step3: In Vikunja, go to Settings > Import from other services and pick Planka
compare.planka.switch.step4: Enter your Planka URL and an API key (or your username and password); credentials are used for the migration only and never stored
compare.planka.switch.step5: Vikunja pulls your projects, boards, cards, labels, checklists, comments, and attachments. Boards become projects, lists become Kanban buckets, done cards stay done
compare.planka.switch.outro: What doesn't come across: assignees, memberships, and avatars, since your team's user accounts don't exist in Vikunja yet. The importer works with Planka v2; for v1 instances it fails with a clear message instead of importing something half right. It ships with the next Vikunja release and is in {unstable} today. See the {help} for details.
compare.planka.cta.text: Point it at your identity provider, bring one board over, and see how it feels.
compare.planka.faq.import.question: Can I import my Planka boards into Vikunja?
compare.planka.faq.import.answer: Yes. Planka has no native export ([open issue]({issueUrl})), only a REST API, so Vikunja's [Planka importer]({importUrl}) talks to that API directly. You enter your Planka URL and an API key (or username and password), and it pulls projects, boards, cards, labels, checklists, comments, and attachments across. Credentials are used for the migration only and never stored. The importer is in unstable builds now and ships with the next release; on [Vikunja Cloud]({pricingUrl}) it's available as soon as the release lands.
compare.planka.faq.sso.question: Is SSO really free in Vikunja?
compare.planka.faq.sso.answer: Yes. [OpenID Connect]({openidUrl}) and [LDAP]({ldapUrl}) are part of the free, self-hosted version and have been for years. Vikunja Pro exists, but it does not gate authentication. The [Pro FAQ]({proUrl}) says it in so many words: you don't need Pro for that.
compare.planka.faq.kanban.question: Does Vikunja have Kanban boards like Planka?
compare.planka.faq.kanban.answer: Yes. Vikunja has a Kanban view with buckets you can create and reorder, plus [List, Gantt, and Table views]({viewsUrl}) on the same data. Planka is a dedicated Kanban tool and does that one thing well. Vikunja gives you Kanban as one of four ways to look at your tasks.
compare.planka.faq.server.question: Can I run Vikunja on the same server as Planka?
compare.planka.faq.server.answer: Yes. Vikunja is a single Go binary or Docker container with SQLite by default (PostgreSQL and MySQL are supported too). It runs alongside an existing Planka install while you migrate. See the [installation guide]({installUrl}).
compare.planka.faq.future.question: Will Vikunja ever move SSO to Pro?
compare.planka.faq.future.answer: The license makes that structurally hard. Vikunja is AGPL-3 with no contributor license agreement, so I don't hold the rights I would need to relicense contributed code. Vikunja Pro ships in the same public repository under the same license. I wrote about why this setup keeps Vikunja open in [Vikunja stays open]({blogUrl}). The same reasoning applies to feature tiering.
compare.planka.faq.lockedOut.question: My Planka admin account was SSO-based and I am locked out. What now?
compare.planka.faq.lockedOut.answer: Planka 2.2.0 deactivates SSO-only users because they no longer have a password login. Planka documents how to [create a new admin user]({adminUrl}) via environment variables, so do that first to regain access and export your data. In Vikunja, OIDC users are regular users: they can be admins, they can be added to teams, and switching auth methods does not deactivate anyone.
